title: Secrets audit & telemetry connector — design notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures design notes and an initial rollout plan for a Secrets Audit & Telemetry Connector (SATC) for Private Deployments. Goal is to provide a lightweight, auditable, and Terraform-friendly integration to link KMS/HSM usage events, envelope-encryption metadata, and secret-access telemetry into our central audit pipeline without leaking plaintext secrets.

Scope:
- Applies to Private (VPC/on-prem) Redwood deployments that use customer-managed KMS or HSMs.
- Covers telemetry design, Terraform module changes, upgrade plan for existing on-prem clusters, verification steps, and rollback strategy.
- Does NOT cover multi-tenant hosted API flows or client-side encryption schemes (will be separate).

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customers may use a mix of cloud KMS, on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11), or vendor-managed HSM appliances.
- We must not transmit plaintext secrets or KV cache contents to the control plane.
- Inter-component communication may traverse private peering/VPN; telemetry must respect network boundaries.
- Terraform is the canonical infra-as-code for deploying connector resources.

Design goals:
1) Auditability: record key events (wrap/unwrap operations, policy changes, key rotations, key import/export attempts) with tamper-evident metadata.
2) Minimal surface area: only metadata and non-secret telemetry leave the customer VPC.
3) Pluggable adapters: support cloud KMS, PKCS#11 HSMs, and vendor APIs via adapters.
4) Terraform-first: customers can opt-in via terraform module flags; changes must be incremental.
5) Backwards-compatible: upgrades should allow staged rollout with canary nodes.

High-level architecture (textual):
- SATC agent runs in customer control plane (DaemonSet) or on a dedicated audit node.
- Agent subscribes to local key manager client library hooks (wrapped by Adapter layer).
- Adapter extracts event metadata: key-id (opaque), operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign), timestamp, principal (service account or node id), request-context (route/model-id), request-id trace id, result-code.
- Agent redacts any PII and signs telemetry bundle with a local attest key (hardware-backed when available).
- Signed telemetry is pushed to the customer-configured audit sink: local syslog, S3-compatible object store, or a queue (Kafka/Rabbit).
- Optional: a secure forwarder (push-proxy) can deliver signed envelopes to Redwood control plane audit collector over mTLS when customer allows.

Data flow notes:
- No ciphertext/plaintext flows to Redwood. Only metadata and attestations.
- Telemetry message example (JSON, pseudocode):
  {
    "key_ref": "projA:keys/enc-1234",
    "op": "decrypt",
    "principal": "svc-model-runtime-7",
    "model_id": "embedder-3-small",
    "timestamp": "2024-12-01T14:22:11Z",
    "req_id": "req-0a1b2c",
    "status": "ok",
    "adapter": "pkcs11-hsm",
    "signature": "BASE64(SIG)",
    "version": "satc-v0.1"
  }
- Important: key_ref must be opaque / non-actionable if exfiltrated. Use hashed key identifiers and optional customer salt stored locally.

Terraform module changes (sketch):
- Module: redwood-private-deployments/secrets-audit-connector
- New flags (variables):
  - enable_satc (bool, default false)
  - satc_mode (string, ["daemonset","dedicated-node"])
  - audit_sink_type (string, ["syslog","s3","kafka","forwarder"])
  - forwarder_endpoint (string)  # only used if audit_sink_type==forwarder
  - adapter_type (string, ["cloudkms","pkcs11","vendor-api"])
  - adapter_config (string, json)  # inline adapter config blob (encrypted in state recommended)
  - attest_key_kms_ref (string) # optional: where the agent stores its attestation key
- Recommended outputs:
  - satc_daemonset_name
  - satc_k8s_service_account
  - satc_tls_secret_name

Terraform state & secret handling notes:
- adapter_config may contain endpoints and paths; DO NOT store raw credentials in module variables. Document practice: use sealed secrets or external secret backends (Vault).
- State file: where possible, mark sensitive = true for outputs and variables. Encourage customers to use remote state backends with encryption at rest.

Upgrade plan (phased):
Phase 0: Preflight (prepare + consent)
- Run preflight script shipped in repo: checks k8s version, node hardware TPM/HSM presence, network egress rules, Terraform version.
- Notify customer: changes will create daemonset + optional forwarder. Get explicit approval for forwarder.
- Create a backup of current cluster state and secrets (existing process).

Phase 1: Canary deploy
- Enable module with enable_satc = true and satc_mode = "daemonset" on 2-3 canary nodes (nodeSelector).
- adapter_type set to "pkcs11" or "cloudkms" based on environment.
- audit_sink_type = "syslog" (local) for canary to avoid external egress.
- Validate events generated for test keys only (use test-key-ids).
- Duration: 48–72 hours of production-like traffic.

Phase 2: Gradual roll-out
- Expand DaemonSet to all non-critical nodes. Start forwarding to configured sink.
- If forwarder is enabled, switch to mTLS and verify chain.
- Validate signed-envelope verification on receiving side (checksum + signature).

Phase 3: Hardening and rotation
- Enable attest_key_kms_ref pointing to customer KMS-wrapped attestation key or HSM-backed key.
- Configure long-term retention rules for audit sinks.

Rollback strategy:
- Terraform destroy the daemonset or set enable_satc=false to stop telemetry injection.
- Remove forwarder endpoints and revoke any ephemeral attest keys that were provisioned.
- Re-run consistency checks to ensure no residual processes are running.

Validation & tests (automation + manual):
- Unit: adapter shim tests with mocked KMS/HSM interfaces.
- Integration: end-to-end test harness in staging that performs wrap/unwrap and asserts telemetry arrives at sink and signature verifies.
- Chaos: simulate HSM latencies and key-unavailability; agent must not block primary KMS operations (fail-open for critical paths must be configurable).
- Compliance checks: ensure key_ref obfuscation and no secret payloads in messages.

Observability & SLOs:
- Telemetry delivery success rate >= 99.9% within 60s (local sink).
- Agent health: report heartbeat metric every 30s.
- Key operation correlation: percent of operations with associated telemetry >= 98% after roll-out.

Operational runbook (quick):
- On alert "satc-agent-down": check DaemonSet pods kubectl -n redwood logs satc-agent-*, restart pod, inspect node PKCS#11 mount.
- On "forwarder-failure": verify forwarder cert, network egress, and mTLS handshake logs.
- On signature verification failures: compare local attest public key vs receiver truststore, rotate attest key if mismatch.

Security considerations:
- Attestation key lifecycle: prefer HSM-backed key for signing telemetry bundles. If not available store attestation key wrapped by customer KMS and restrict IAM.
- Least privilege: agent SA should have minimal permissions: list/describe keys only if needed for metadata; never get raw key material.
- Rate limiting: ensure agent cannot create large burst traffic to forwarder/sink; guardrails in Terraform.
- Data sovereignty: allow sink selection within customer region and support offline collection for air-gapped environments.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Should we version telemetry schema at adapter level or agent level? (Proposal: agent semantic version + adapter minor version).
- Q: How to standardize hashed key_ref across cloud KMS vendors? Need consistent salt handling.
- TODO: add explicit Terraform examples for Vault sealed-secret integration.
- TODO: define canonical RBAC policy for the satc_k8s_service_account.
- TODO: create compliance checklist (SOC2 / ISO) entry with legal.

Risks:
- Misconfigured forwarder could expose metadata externally — mitigate by defaults: forwarder disabled, syslog only.
- Poorly redacted key_refs could leak internal naming — implement mandatory hashing + length limit.

Appendix: quick examples and commands
- Preflight script: ./tools/satc/preflight.sh --kube-context prod-cluster --adapter pkcs11
- Check telemetry in sink (local syslog): sudo journalctl -u satc-forwarder -f
- Verify signature (receiver): cat msg.json | satc-verify --pubkey /etc/satc/trust/pub.pem

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc lightweight; target a short RFC for eng-review next week.
- Coordinate with SRE for rollout window (narrow maintenance window).
- Liaise with Solutions Eng for customer-facing upgrade notes and sample Terraform snippets.

Next steps:
1) Convert this into RFC and get reviews from SRE, Security, and Solutions Eng.
2) Implement minimal adapter interface and unit tests.
3) Draft Terraform example and a short migration playbook for customers.

References:
- Internal: Confluence Secrets Lifecycle Hub (see linked_artifacts).
- External: PKCS#11 best practices, RFC 6234 (signature encapsulation)

End of notes.
summary: Design notes and rollout plan for a Secrets Audit & Telemetry Connector for private deployments, including Terraform module sketches, phased upgrade plan, validation and runbook items.
